text: The Science: Eating more potassium brings high blood pressure down (Aburto, et al, 2013), which matters on Strategy A, since its salts bring their own sodium. If you have kidney disease or take a blood pressure drug that holds on to potassium, like an ACE inhibitor or an ARB, ask your doctor first, since potassium can build up in your blood (NIH, 2022).
reader: someone with trauma or in withdrawal who is anxious, wired, numb or foggy, following the protocol's diet and electrolyte steps and wanting to know why each one is there

checked.point: low potassium (common in high stress) makes the KCNQ brakes fail, and eating potassium puts them back
checked.found: the brain keeps the potassium around its neurons within tight limits whatever the blood does (Hladky and Barrand 2016; dogs: Javaheri and Kazemi 1981), so neither the drop stress brings to the blood (Brown 1983) nor what you eat sets the brakes
checked.still_needed: no: the brakes story is cut, with its two labels (blocks 104 and 105)

checked.point: eating more potassium brings high blood pressure down
checked.found: in trials, more potassium lowered systolic pressure by about 3.5 mm Hg, in people with high blood pressure and not in others (Aburto et al. 2013)
checked.still_needed: yes: they learn why the target and the foods that follow are there on Strategy A

checked.point: kidney disease and drugs that keep potassium in can let it build up
checked.found: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce urinary potassium excretion, which can lead to hyperkalemia, and experts recommend monitoring (NIH 2022); in kidney disease, restricting potassium slowed neuropathy over two years (Arnold et al. 2017)
checked.still_needed: yes: they ask their doctor before eating more potassium if either applies to them

checked.point: potassium-rich food supports normal nerve function (GPT's version)
checked.found: the potassium gradient is required for nerve transmission, but hypokalemia is rarely caused by low dietary intake alone (NIH 2022)
checked.still_needed: no: eating more doesn't change nerve function unless something has drained potassium, so it isn't a reason the paragraph gives
